title: The source norm of a target pullback is groupoid-invariant
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose morphisms $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] make $U(H)$ and $R(H)$ the objects and arrows of a groupoid, functorially in every test scheme $H$, with the indicated source, target, identity, inverse and composition. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and put $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$ and $C=\{a\in A:\sigma(a)=\tau(a)\}$. For $b\in B$, let $N_\sigma(b)\in A$ be the norm section of [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts]: on every affine open where $B$ via $\sigma$ is finite free it is the determinant of multiplication by $b$ [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. Then for every $f\in A$,
$$N_\sigma(\tau(f))\in C,$$
that is, $\sigma(N_\sigma(\tau(f)))=\tau(N_\sigma(\tau(f)))$. No constant-rank, reducedness or freeness of the arrow relation is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03BH (groupoids-lemma-determinant-trick); norm construction in Divisors Tag 0BD2 (divisors-lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), applied locally on rank strata.

proof.text: Put $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$ with projections $p_0,p_1$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. The groupoid identities give $s\circ c=s\circ p_1$ and $t\circ c=t\circ p_0$. The square with top map $p_0$, bottom map $t$, and vertical maps $p_1,s$ is the defining pullback. The square with top map $c$, bottom map $s$, and the same vertical maps $p_1,s$ is also a pullback: the morphism $P\to R\times_{s,U,s}R$ sending $(a,b)$ to $(c(a,b),b)$ has inverse $(h,b)\mapsto(c(h,i(b)),b)$. Both composites are identities by associativity and the inverse and identity laws; these are morphisms by the fibre-product universal property. Thus $p_1:P\to R$ is the pullback of $s$ along $t$ via $p_0$, and along $s$ via $c$. For $a=t^\sharp(f)$, the identity $t\circ c=t\circ p_0$ gives $c^\sharp(a)=p_0^\sharp(a)$.

source.place: groupoids-lemma-diagram, explicit inverse for the lower right square; Tag 03BH (groupoids-lemma-determinant-trick), first equality

proof.text: Write $n=N_\sigma(a)$ and use [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts] to cover $U$ by affine opens $V$ where the section algebra of $s^{-1}(V)$ is finite free and $n|_V$ is its multiplication determinant. Refine the intersections $s^{-1}(V_s)\cap t^{-1}(V_t)$ by affine opens $W$ of $R$. On $W$, the two squares in step 1 identify the algebra of $p_1^{-1}(W)$ respectively with the scalar extensions of the section algebras over $V_s$ and $V_t$; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives these tensor-product identifications and their maps. A basis $(e_j)$ of either chart algebra becomes the basis $(e_j\otimes1)$ after extension to $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_R)$. If $a e_j=\sum_i m_{ij}e_i$, then $(a\otimes1)(e_j\otimes1)=\sum_i g^\sharp(m_{ij})(e_i\otimes1)$, with $g=s$ or $t$ on the relevant chart. By [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], the determinant is $g^\sharp(\det(m_{ij}))$: the ring map preserves each sum, sign and product in the Leibniz formula. Consequently $(s^\sharp n)|_W$ is the determinant of multiplication by $c^\sharp(a)$ on $\Gamma(p_1^{-1}(W),\mathcal O_P)$ in the first pulled-back basis, and $(t^\sharp n)|_W$ is the determinant of multiplication by $p_0^\sharp(a)$ on that same algebra in the second basis.

source.place: Tag 03BH (groupoids-lemma-determinant-trick), the two norm base-change equalities; Tag 02DV (exercises-exercise-trace-det-rings)(1),(3); Tag 0BD2 (divisors-lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), determinant construction on each chart

proof.text: On each $W$ from step 2, the two multiplication endomorphisms are equal because $c^\sharp(a)=p_0^\sharp(a)$ by step 1. Their determinants agree even in the two different bases, by the basis independence stated in [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. Therefore $(s^\sharp n)|_W=(t^\sharp n)|_W$. These $W$ cover $R$, so the sheaf equality axiom for its structure sheaf [def-pc-scheme] gives $s^\sharp n=t^\sharp n$ in $B$. The defining equality for $C$ now says $n=N_\sigma(\tau(f))\in C$. All calculations are on finite-free charts and allow different ranks on different components; the empty matrix has determinant $1$, so no positive-rank assumption has entered.

lean.statement: theorem affineGroupoid_invariant_norm (A B : CommRingCat.{u}) (s t : Spec B ⟶ Spec A) (e : Spec A ⟶ Spec B) (i : Spec B ⟶ Spec B) (c : pullback s t ⟶ Spec B) (hG : Scheme.IsGroupoid s t e i c) [s.IsFiniteLocallyFree] [t.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (f n : A) (hn : ∀ x : Spec A, ∃ V : (Spec A).Opens, x ∈ V ∧ IsAffineOpen V ∧ (letI := (s.app V).hom.toAlgebra Module.Free Γ(Spec A, V) Γ(Spec B, s ⁻¹ᵁ V) ∧ Module.Finite Γ(Spec A, V) Γ(Spec B, s ⁻¹ᵁ V) ∧ (Spec A).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv n) = Algebra.norm Γ(Spec A, V) ((Spec B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : s ⁻¹ᵁ V ≤ ⊤)).op ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso B).inv ((Spec.preimage t).hom f))))) : n ∈ RingHom.eqLocus (Spec.preimage s).hom (Spec.preimage t).hom
lean.note: The norm section n is specified by the local finite-free determinant charts of exists_finiteLocallyFree_norm_charts, transported through Scheme.ΓSpecIso. No global freeness or constant-rank hypothesis is imposed.
